arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Miller argued the agency reasonably interpreted the Act to require state inheritance proof.
Mr. Rothfeld argued the statute unambiguously dictates the family's reading without state law references.
Chief Justice Roberts asked how the agency handles new reproductive technologies where state law is unclear.
Justice Alito suggested Congress may have assumed a clear definition of child without needing state law.

case_history.explanation: An official oral-argument transcript was verified.

case.dek: The dispute centers on whether federal law requires applicants to prove state inheritance rights to receive child survivor benefits.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Social Security Administration interprets the Social Security Act to require proof of state inheritance eligibility. The Capato family argues the statute unambiguously defines eligibility without referencing state law. The government contends state intestacy law provides a reasonable standard for determining child status.

sections.heading: How the case got here
paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on March 19, 2012.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The government wants the Court to uphold the use of state inheritance law as the eligibility standard.
The family wants the Court to reject the state law requirement and grant benefits based on federal definitions.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues the Social Security Act reasonably incorporates state intestacy law to define child status.
The family argues the statute is unambiguous and does not reference state inheritance law for eligibility.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Ginsburg asked about the meaning of a specific statutory provision regarding state law status.
Justice Kagan questioned why Congress defined stepchildren without referencing state intestacy law in other sections.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines how federal agencies define family relationships for benefit eligibility. It clarifies the relationship between federal benefits and state inheritance laws. The outcome affects millions of families seeking survivor benefits. It establishes a standard for interpreting statutory definitions of family status.
